sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was discovered between 1917 and 1919 in Jabalpur, India, by Charles Alfred Matley.
Indosaurus matleyi was named by Huene and Matley in 1933, making it the first majungasaurine discovered.
Indosaurus lived alongside sauropods such as Isisaurus and Jainosaurus, which it may have preyed upon.
Indosaurus was originally assigned to Allosauridae but is now considered a member of the Abelisauridae family.
Indosaurus lived in what is now India between 69 and 66 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous.
The Lameta Formation rocks where Indosaurus fossils were found were deposited in fluvial or lacustrine conditions.
The time range for Indosaurus is estimated from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
Some paleontologists speculate that Indosuchus, Lametasaurus, and Indosaurus should be considered nomina dubia.
